t:
(a) 

        (1) 
Section 223(d) of the Social Security Act is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new paragraph:


“(6)

(A) 
Notwithstanding any other provision of this title, any physical or mental impairment which arises in connection with the commission by an individual (after the date of the enactment of this paragraph) of an offense which constitutes a felony under applicable law and for which such individual is subsequently convicted, or which is aggravated in connection with such an offense (but only to the extent so aggravated), shall not be considered in determining whether an individual is under a disability.


“(B) 
Notwithstanding any other provision of this title, any physical or mental impairment which arises in connection with an individual’s confinement in a jail, prison, or other penal institution or correctional facility pursuant to such individual’s conviction of an offense (committed after the date of the enactment of this paragraph) constituting a felony under applicable law, or which is aggravated in connection with such a confinement (but only to the extent so aggravated), shall not be considered in determining whether such individual is under a disability for purposes of benefits payable for any month during which such individual is so confined.”.



 
        (2) 
The third sentence of section 216(i)(1) of such Act is amended by striking out “and (5)” and inserting in lieu thereof “(5), and (6)”.
  
    (b) 
Section 202(d)(7)(A) of such Act is amended by adding at the end thereof the following: “An individual shall not be considered a ‘full-time student’ for the purpose of this section while that individual is confined in a jail, prison, or other penal institution or correctional facility, pursuant to his conviction of an offense (committed after the date of the enactment of this paragraph) which constituted a felony under applicable law.”.
 
    (c) 
Section 223 of such Act is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new subsection:

“Suspension of Benefits for Inmates of Penal Institutions
“(f) 

(1) 
Notwithstanding any other provision of this title, no monthly benefits shall be paid under this section, or under section 202(d) by reason of being under a disability, to any individual for any month during which such individual is confined in a jail, prison, or other penal institution or correctional facility, pursuant to his conviction of an offense which constituted a felony under applicable law, unless such individual is actively and satisfactorily participating in a rehabilitation program which has been specifically approved for such individual by a court of law and, as determined by the Secretary, is expected to result in such individual being able to engage in substantial gainful activity upon release and within a reasonable time.


“(2) 
Benefits which would be payable to any individual (other than a confined individual to whom benefits are not payable by reason of paragraph (1)) under this title on the basis of the wages and self-employment income of such a confined individual but for the provisions of paragraph (1), shall be payable as though such confined individual were receiving such benefits under this section.”.



 
    (d) 
The amendments made by this section shall be effective with respect to benefits payable for months beginning on or after October 1, 1980.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "participating in a rehabilitation program" signals participation, but that phrase describes an inmate's eligibility condition for benefits, not outside parties being consulted on a federal decision. The section only restricts disability and student benefits for people convicted of felonies or confined in penal institutions. It provides no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, rulemaking authority, or right to sue.
fable.s: unless such individual is actively and satisfactorily participating in a rehabilitation program which has been specifically approved for such individual by a court of law

qwen_block.w: The section defines eligibility criteria for Social Security benefits, specifically excluding individuals confined for felonies unless they participate in a court-approved rehabilitation program. This is a condition for receiving a benefit, not a mechanism for outside parties to consult with or influence federal decision-making. The 'participation' mentioned refers to the inmate's engagement in a program, not public participation in government policy.
qwen_block.s: unless such individual is actively and satisfactorily participating in a rehabilitation program which has been specifically approved for such individual by a court of law

opus.w: This section changes Social Security disability and student-benefit eligibility for convicted felons, and it suspends benefits for inmates. The word 'participating' describes an inmate's enrollment in a rehabilitation program as a condition for getting benefits. It is not outside parties being consulted on a federal decision. Benefit eligibility and applications are excluded from the definition. The section has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
opus.s: unless such individual is actively and satisfactorily participating in a rehabilitation program which has been specifically approved for such individual by a court of law and, as determined by the Secretary, is expected to result in such individual being able to engage in substantial gainful activity upon release
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section says an inmate is "actively and satisfactorily participating in a rehabilitation program" approved "by a court of law." That could look like participation. It isn't. The word refers to an inmate taking part in rehabilitation as a condition for receiving benefits. Nobody outside the government is consulted or given a voice before a federal decision. This is a benefits-eligibility rule, and benefits are excluded under the definition.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines eligibility criteria for Social Security benefits, specifically suspending benefits for inmates unless they participate in a court-approved rehabilitation program. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants' from the scope of participation. The 'participation' mentioned is a condition for receiving a benefit, not a process where outside parties consult with or influence federal decision-making. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: unless such individual is actively and satisfactorily participating in a rehabilitation program which has been specifically approved for such individual by a court of law and, as determined by the Secretary, is expected to result in such individual being able to engage in substantial gainful activity upon release and within a reasonable time.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for an inmate to be "actively and satisfactorily participating in a rehabilitation program" constitutes participation because it involves an outside party (the inmate) engaging in a process that affects their benefits. However, the definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." Determining eligibility for benefits based on participation in a program is part of the benefits determination process, not a mechanism for outside parties to consult with or influence federal decision-making. The "participation" here is a condition for receiving a benefit, not a form of public input into government policy or decisions.
